# Synthetic source references

Every record, field choice, page boundary, response body and CSV byte in these fixtures was authored for testing. No Airtable account, live API, credential, or real export was used. The fixture corpus does not claim parity with a vendor export.

Public documentation links used as source-format references:

- [Airtable Web API introduction](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/introduction)
- [Airtable list records endpoint](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/list-records)
- [Airtable base schema endpoint](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/get-base-schema)
- [Airtable field and table IDs](https://support.airtable.com/docs/field-and-table-ids)
- [Airtable linked record fields](https://support.airtable.com/docs/linked-record-field)
- [Airtable CSV export guidance](https://support.airtable.com/docs/airtable-views)

The exact source details used here are deliberately stated as fixture assumptions where public documentation is silent or presentation can vary:

- CSV sets contain one `<table label>-Grid view.csv` file per included table. A preview maps each filename to its editable destination table label. Each file is RFC 4180-style UTF-8 with a header row; the first header is the primary field. Fixture CSV files use CRLF record separators. The edge fixture's `Targets-Grid view.csv` additionally starts with a UTF-8 BOM.
- A CSV link cell is a comma-separated list of destination primary labels with no padding whitespace around the delimiter. A token containing a comma or double quote is enclosed in double quotes; a double quote inside a token is doubled. The cell is then quoted and escaped again by the outer CSV format. No whitespace trimming, case folding, or first-match lookup is permitted; any whitespace present inside a token is significant. A duplicate primary label is ambiguous and remains unlinked; a label with no exact match is unresolved.
- Per-column counts are hand-accounted from these exact source cells and mappings. `sourceValues` counts nonempty source cells. `converted` counts cells whose source/native representation changes, once per cell even if it contains several link references; this includes a type change or canonical textual change, plus blank/omitted values mapped to native `null` or `[]`. An explicit empty API link array would remain unchanged, but these files use blank CSV cells or omitted API link fields. `textChanges` counts changed text renderings: CSV label links and checkbox cells count, structured API ID arrays mapped to native links and omitted API values do not. Select labels mapped to opaque native option IDs count as conversions and text changes. `keptText` counts nonempty source values retained in a native text field, including joined API multi-select labels. `notRecreated` names nonempty formula/rollup values or a skipped missing-target field; `skippedNonempty` counts every nonempty cell in an explicitly skipped field. Link-reference totals still enumerate every raw link token, independently of per-cell conversion counts.
- Each reciprocal pair has one physical native link field; the opposite table exposes a derived incoming-relation projection that points to the canonical field. The mapping declares the reciprocal owner choice, while hand-written `derivedIncomingRelationValues` separately states the expected projected display. When both source sides are present, the side with cardinality `one` is canonical. If both sides have cardinality `many`, the earlier table in source metadata order is canonical. If both sides have cardinality `one`, the earlier table in source metadata order is canonical. Noncanonical source cells remain counted and compared; disagreement is reported without changing the canonical links. These rules are authored for these fixtures and are not claimed as vendor behavior.
- The CRM lookup is recalculated through the deal's Company relation to the Company primary field. Source lookup text is evidence for comparison only; it is not a writable value. Select option order in CSV expectations follows first appearance in row order, followed by any explicit owner-preview choices. API source metadata choices and unused-option accounting are retained as source evidence; without an explicit owner choice, native select options follow first-seen nonempty row values. The CSV owner-preview choice list is explicit and may add choices that values alone cannot reveal.
- CRM checkbox cells use the explicit CSV convention `checked` = true and empty = false. The CRM view has four checked cells and five empty cells; API pages retain four explicit true booleans and omit five false values. `sourceValues` counts the four nonempty checked cells. All nine CSV row cells change representation to Boolean; on the API path the four explicit true cells already match, while each of the five omitted false values changes to Boolean false. This convention is hand-authored and is not claimed as vendor export behavior.
- Currency source cells retain the exact two-decimal display strings in CSV and JSON number bytes in API pages. Expected native numeric strings use canonical exact decimal notation: remove grouping and currency display syntax, divide displayed percentages by 100, omit insignificant trailing fractional zeroes and the trailing decimal point, and preserve exact value. The CRM fixture has five nonempty currency values and three percentage fractions per path (eight value normalizations); its three Employees values retain the same digit strings. CSV Employee cells are already canonical text and have no representation conversion; the three API Employee numbers change type to exact decimal strings with unchanged digits. For example `$1,250,000.00` and API number `1250000` both map to `1250000`, while `60%` and API fraction `0.6` both map to `0.6`. No binary floating-point or currency conversion is implied. Date-only cells remain ISO calendar dates.
- API list responses use synthetic IDs and exact response bytes in the captured-page order listed by each `manifest.json`. `offset` values are synthetic pagination tokens. Empty API `fields` objects are omitted; an omitted checkbox means false. Linked-record fields carry arrays of source record IDs. Percent values are fractions. A relation whose `linkedTableId` is absent from metadata remains an unresolved reference; the fixture does not imply that a full-base export always omits target tables. API lookup values are arrays: the CRM has one recognized lookup column and three rows with one-element label arrays; each array is compared to the scalar label recomputed through its canonical Company link, and all three match. Multi-value lookup behavior is not asserted.
- The Project tracker maps four multiple-select arrays to native text by joining labels in their original order with comma plus space: `Planning, Needs review`, `Finance`, `Research, Needs review`, and `Build, Documentation`. The CSV strings already have those exact native text values; the API arrays are retained byte-for-byte and each array-to-text conversion is named in the API expectation. Its unused `Legacy` multi-select option is explicitly retained in source-option accounting, not recreated as a native choice. Formula and rollup fields are retained as named source fields but are not recreated, attachment fields are skipped and counted when nonempty, and no formula/rollup engine or attachment object store is implied. Due at values are authored as complete ISO instants and mapped to text byte-for-byte; this does not assert how a live export formats date-time values.
- CRM Contacts.Website is a source URL field mapped to native text; all three example.com values are kept exactly without URL validation or normalization.
- Formula-looking and HTML-looking strings in the Edges fixture are inert source text. Its retained `json/base-snapshot-v1.json` is deliberately a negative sample, not a successful import: it uses `{ "format": "cradle-base-v1" }` without the required `version: 1` envelope, references absent target record `recSYN00000000888`, and references absent target table `tblSYN00000000999`. Its handwritten expectation is rejection before writes. Only the CSV and recorded API paths are successful Edges fixtures; no JSON roundtrip result is claimed.
- Source table, field, and record IDs use reserved synthetic shapes. Native table, field, option, incoming-relation, and record ULIDs are intentionally not guessed in expected data. Consumers bind each symbolic identity once to the IDs allocated by the reviewed native preview and compare through that explicit binding.

`manifest.json`, `mapping.json`, `ground-truth.json`, and the expected files next to each source describe the exact raw paths, symbolic records, owner-preview choices, path differences, and counts.

## Attachment cells (`attachments/`)

`attachments/csv/Assets-Grid view.csv` is authored, not exported. Airtable's view guide says "Attachment fields will be included in the CSV file as a filename and URL", and its attachment URL guide extracts a file name as the text before `(`. The cells are written to that shape as `file name (https URL)`, with several files separated by comma and space. Airtable does not publish the separator for several files, so that part is an authored assumption; a real export may differ, and Cradle lists any cell that does not read as that shape with its raw text only. Row 2 holds two files, row 3 a comma inside a file name, row 4 an empty cell and row 5 a file name with no URL. All URLs use the reserved `example.com` domain. `expected.json` is the hand-written expectation.

- [Airtable views and CSV download](https://support.airtable.com/articles/5189551686-getting-started-with-airtable-views)
- [Airtable attachment URL behavior](https://support.airtable.com/articles/9671148410-airtable-attachment-url-behavior)
